Sūrat al-Muʾmin. The Sunna gives this sūra the name «Ḥā Mīm al-Muʾmin»: al-Tirmidhī reports from Abū Hurayra that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, «Whoever recites Ḥā Mīm al-Muʾmin up to “to Him is the final return”, along with Āyat al-Kursī, in the morning, is kept safe by the two of them…» and the rest of the ḥadīth.", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:1"}, {"n": 2, "ar": "وبِذَلِكَ اشْتُهِرَتْ في مَصاحِفِ المَشْرِقِ،", "en": "That is the name it is best known by in the muṣḥafs of the East,", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:2"}, {"n": 3, "ar": "وبِذَلِكَ تَرْجَمَها البُخارِيُّ في صَحِيحِهِ والتِّرْمِذِيُّ في الجامِعِ.", "en": "and it is also the title al-Bukhārī gives its chapter in his Ṣaḥīḥ, and al-Tirmidhī in his Jāmiʿ.", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:3"}, {"n": 4, "ar": "ووَجْهُ التَّسْمِيَةِ أنَّها ذُكِرَتْ فِيها قِصَّةُ مُؤْمِنِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ ولَمْ تُذْكَرْ في سُورَةٍ أُخْرى بِوَجْهٍ صَرِيحٍ.", "en": "It got this name because it tells the story of the believer from Pharaoh's people, a story no other sūra tells openly.", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:4"}, {"n": 5, "ar": "والوَجْهُ في إعْرابِ هَذا الِاسْمِ حِكايَةُ كَلِمَةِ (حم) ساكِنَةَ المِيمِ بِلَفْظِها الَّذِي يُقْرَأُ.", "en": "Grammatically, the best way to treat this name is to keep the word «Ḥā Mīm» exactly as it is recited, with a silent mīm,", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:5"}, {"n": 6, "ar": "وبِإضافَتِهِ إلى لَفْظِ (المُؤْمِنِ) بِتَقْدِيرِ: سُورَةُ حم ذِكْرِ المُؤْمِنِ أوْ لَفْظِ المُؤْمِنِ وتُسَمّى أيْضًا (سُورَةُ الطَّوْلِ) لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى في أوَّلِها (ذِي الطَّوْلِ) وقَدْ تُنُوسِيَ هَذا الِاسْمُ.", "en": "and to join it to the word «al-Muʾmin», understood as “the Ḥā Mīm sūra that mentions the Believer”, or “that has the word al-Muʾmin”. It was also called “Sūrat al-Ṭawl”, from the words “Lord of bounty” near its start, but that name has fallen out of use.", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:6"}, {"n": 7, "ar": "وتُسَمّى سُورَةُ غافِرٍ لِذِكْرِ وصْفِهِ تَعالى (غافِرِ الذَّنْبِ) في أوَّلِها.", "en": "It is also called Sūrat Ghāfir, because it opens by describing Allah as “Forgiver of sin”.", "ref": "TS:ibn_ashur:40:intro:r1:7"}]}}
